rationale: A wins because it keeps the ambition without pretending the missing facts are facts. "Wise will roll out stablecoin settlement one regulator at a time" is a real policy story and it names the facts needed before pitching; B's "The businesses waiting three days for a payment that clears in minutes" manufactures the most clickable part of the story. B has good reporter targeting, but it keeps stepping over the evidence line, especially with "balance-sheet flows."
gaps_in_A: "the first-market decision is the news" rests on a market name the update does not supply; A asks for it, but the angle still leans on an absent first market.

"A listed, profitable payments company is now settling business transfers in stablecoin" is strong but close to category overreach until the stablecoin, partner, launch markets, and volume share are named.
"Investors will ask what stablecoin settlement does to Wise's margins" is plausible, not proven; it needs analyst reaction or CFO evidence before it becomes a markets pitch.
"over £30B a quarter" is total cross-border volume, not stated business-payment or stablecoin-eligible volume; A should require that split more explicitly.
gaps_in_B: "A profitable listed payments company is putting stablecoins on its balance-sheet flows" overstates the facts; the update says businesses can hold and settle, not that Wise holds stablecoins on its own balance sheet.
"The businesses waiting three days for a payment that clears in minutes" invents both the old delay and the new clearance time. That is not color; that is fakery in a better suit.
"they can bypass the bank-to-bank rail for part of that flow" smuggles in eligible-share and rail-replacement assumptions before Wise has said whether this replaces or supplements anything.
"the first time this flow is being described as a shipped feature rather than a position" adds a prior-history claim the update does not provide.
